**Question 2.** Which combinations of patient characteristics and treatments are associated with early
readmission?

This document uses association rule mining on the cleaned data from Part 1 (render
`01_data_preparation_eda.Rmd` first). The Python version is `python/03_q2_association_rules.ipynb`.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
# ---- Setup ----
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(arules)

theme_set(theme_minimal())
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5)

df <- read.csv("../data/processed/diabetes_clean_r.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = "")
dim(df)
```

# 1. Approach

The approach mirrors the Python version:

- **Transactions:** each patient becomes one basket of 16 items, one per attribute. Numeric features are
  discretized into a few clinically sensible bins, because Apriori works on categorical items.
- **Measures:** *support* (share of all patients with both sides of the rule), *confidence* (the
  readmission rate within the group on the left-hand side) and *lift* (confidence ÷ the overall 8.98%
  rate).
- **Settings:** Apriori with minimum support 0.5% and at most 4 items per rule, keeping only rules whose
  right-hand side is `readmit_30=yes`. Lift ≥ 1.5 marks higher-risk groups; lift ≤ 0.67 marks
  lower-risk groups.
- **Redundancy:** a rule is kept only if its confidence is higher (risk rules) or lower (low-risk rules)
  than that of every shorter rule contained in it.

```{r transactions}
bin <- function(x, breaks, labels) as.character(cut(x, breaks, labels = labels, right = FALSE))

items <- data.frame(
  age             = bin(df$age_years, c(0, 60, 80, 200), c("<60", "60-79", "80+")),
  gender          = df$gender,
  admission       = df$admission_type,
  source          = df$admission_source,
  discharge       = df$discharge_to,
  diag1           = df$diag1_group,
  stay            = bin(df$time_in_hospital, c(0, 4, 8, 99), c("1-3 days", "4-7 days", "8+ days")),
  prior_inpatient = bin(df$number_inpatient, c(0, 1, 2, 999), c("0", "1", "2+")),
  prior_emergency = ifelse(df$number_emergency > 0, "1+", "0"),
  diagnoses       = bin(df$number_diagnoses, c(0, 7, 9, 99), c("<7", "7-8", "9+")),
  medications     = bin(df$num_medications, c(0, 11, 21, 999), c("<11", "11-20", "21+")),
  A1C             = dplyr::recode(df$A1Cresult, ">7" = "high", ">8" = "high", "None" = "not tested",
                                  "Norm" = "normal"),
  insulin         = ifelse(df$insulin == "No", "no", "yes"),
  med_change      = ifelse(df$change == "Ch", "yes", "no"),
  diabetes_med    = tolower(df$diabetesMed),
  readmit_30      = ifelse(df$readmit_30 == 1, "yes", "no"),
  stringsAsFactors = TRUE
)

# Each column becomes items named 'column=value', e.g. 'discharge=Home'
trans <- as(items, "transactions")
trans
```

# 2. Mining the rules

```{r apriori}
rules <- apriori(trans,
                 parameter = list(support = 0.005, confidence = 0, minlen = 1, maxlen = 4),
                 appearance = list(rhs = "readmit_30=yes", default = "lhs"),
                 control = list(verbose = FALSE))
base_rate <- mean(items$readmit_30 == "yes")
cat(sprintf("Rules with consequent readmit_30=yes: %s (base rate %.2f%%)\n",
            format(length(rules), big.mark = ","), base_rate * 100))
```

```{r redundancy}
q <- quality(rules)
q$lhs <- labels(lhs(rules))
q$size <- size(lhs(rules))
conf <- setNames(q$confidence, q$lhs)
conf["{}"] <- base_rate

# Confidence of every proper subset of a rule's left-hand side
subset_confs <- function(lhs_label) {
  parts <- strsplit(gsub("^\\{|\\}$", "", lhs_label), ",")[[1]]
  if (length(parts) == 0 || parts[1] == "") return(numeric(0))
  subs <- unlist(lapply(0:(length(parts) - 1), function(k) {
    if (k == 0) return("{}")
    apply(combn(parts, k), 2, function(s) paste0("{", paste(s, collapse = ","), "}"))
  }))
  conf[subs[subs %in% names(conf)]]
}

tidy <- function(d) {
  d %>%
    transmute(rule = gsub(",", ", ", lhs), patients = round(coverage * length(trans)),
              support = round(support, 3), confidence = round(confidence, 3), lift = round(lift, 3))
}

high <- q %>% filter(lift >= 1.5)
high <- high[mapply(function(l, c) all(c > subset_confs(l)), high$lhs, high$confidence), ]
high <- tidy(arrange(high, desc(lift)))

low <- q %>% filter(lift <= 0.67)
low <- low[mapply(function(l, c) all(c < subset_confs(l)), low$lhs, low$confidence), ]
low <- tidy(arrange(low, lift))

cat("Higher-risk rules (lift >= 1.5):", nrow(high), "non-redundant, from", sum(q$lift >= 1.5), "\n")
cat("Lower-risk rules (lift <= 0.67):", nrow(low), "non-redundant, from", sum(q$lift <= 0.67), "\n")
```

head(low, 10)

```{r scatter}
ggplot(q, aes(support, confidence, colour = lift)) +
  geom_point(size = 1, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = base_rate, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_colour_gradient2(low = "steelblue", mid = "grey85", high = "firebrick", midpoint = 1) +
  labs(title = "Association Rules with Consequent {readmit_30 = yes}",
       x = "Support: share of all patients (log scale)",
       y = "Confidence (readmission rate in the group)", colour = "Lift")
```

```{r top-rules, fig.height = 6}
show <- rbind(head(high, 8) %>% mutate(kind = "Higher risk"),
              head(low, 5) %>% mutate(kind = "Lower risk"))
ggplot(show, aes(x = reorder(rule, confidence), y = confidence, fill = kind)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = base_rate, linetype = "dashed") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Higher risk" = "firebrick", "Lower risk" = "steelblue")) +
  labs(title = "Strongest Non-Redundant Rules", x = "Rule antecedent",
       y = "Confidence: 30-day readmission rate in the group", fill = NULL)
```

```{r save}
write.csv(high, "../report/figures/q2_high_risk_rules_r.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(low, "../report/figures/q2_low_risk_rules_r.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# 3. Discussion

The R rules match the Python version, since both run Apriori on the same baskets with the same
thresholds. There are `r nrow(high)` non-redundant higher-risk rules and `r nrow(low)` lower-risk ones.

- **Repeated hospital use** gives the strongest rules: patients with two or more inpatient stays in the
  previous year are readmitted within 30 days at
  `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * conf["{prior_inpatient=2+}"])`, `r round(conf["{prior_inpatient=2+}"] / base_rate, 2)`
  times the average.
- **Discharge to a care facility**, especially for patients aged 60–79, emergency admissions and
  circulatory diagnoses, gives readmission rates of about 17–19% (lift about 2).
- **Younger patients with no prior stay** who are discharged home with few diagnoses or medications have
  the lowest rates, about 5% (lift about 0.56–0.59).

These groups echo the two strongest predictors from Question 1 (prior inpatient visits and discharge
destination) and show where the risk concentrates. The rules depend on the chosen bins and minimum
support, and they describe co-occurrence, not cause.
